# HELMET

> HELMET is a small PHP package that sends the security headers and a nonce-based CSP, hardens the session, checks the proxy, answers /up and writes JSON logs. Raw PHP, Laravel and PSR-15 apps all use the same core.

GIF via [Tenor](https://tenor.com/view/helmet-band-wilmas-rainbow-helmet-band-music-gif-25658120)

**Put it on before you ship.** Security headers, a hardened session and an honest proxy check, snapped on before
the first page is served.

Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub).
Two mirrors, one command: the only thing in this repo that plays both sides is the CI.
Front page: [`site/index.html`](https://github.com/waynestate/helmet/blob/HEAD/site/index.html), the playbook, as static files ([`site/README.md`](https://github.com/waynestate/helmet/blob/HEAD/site/README.md)).
On Citadel it is served by the raw-PHP deploy layer in [`deploy/`](https://github.com/waynestate/helmet/blob/HEAD/deploy/): a Squire kit whose front controller serves `site/` behind HELMET's security headers. For local development, keep serving `site/` directly.
Documentation: [helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/) carries the overview and the environment variables the package reads, with more pages on the way.

HELMET is the Wayne State app stack's baseline runtime. One small
framework-free PHP core, `Waynestate\Helmet`, does the five things every app on
Citadel needs before it serves a single page: it sends the security headers,
hardens the session, decides whether the request really arrived over HTTPS,
answers the load balancer's `/up` ping, and writes structured logs.

Every page below is Markdown. The HTML pages send the same Markdown to a client that asks for `text/markdown`. Written by Squire's agent-ready kit from the README and the pages; do not edit.

## Pages

- [HELMET: Put it on before you ship.](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/index.md): HELMET is a small PHP package that sends the security headers and a nonce-based CSP, hardens the session, checks the proxy, answers /up and writes JSON logs. Raw PHP, Laravel and PSR-15 apps all use the same core.
- [Changelog | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/changelog.md): All notable changes to this project.
- [Cross-origin isolation and feature policy | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/cross-origin-isolation.md): Three more headers round out the baseline: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy and Permissions-Policy are on by default, Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy is opt-in.
- [Customizing the CSP | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csp.md): A csp policy passed to helmet_boot() or the middleware is merged over the default, per directive.
- [The request-forgery guard | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/csrf.md): SameSite=Lax is a layer, not a wall: the optional request-forgery guard checks state-changing requests before they reach the app.
- [The headers | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/headers.md): Every response gets the same set of security headers, built by one shared function.
- [Configuring HSTS | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/hsts.md): The default HSTS is max-age=31536000 with includeSubDomains, sent on HTTPS responses only, and it rolls out in stages.
- [HTTPS, and why the proxy list matters | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/https-and-proxies.md): HELMET honors X-Forwarded-Proto only when the connection came from a trusted proxy, so a spoofed header is ignored and no HSTS goes out for a request that was not really secure.
- [Strongly recommended: a git.wayne.edu instance runner | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/instance-runner.md): git.wayne.edu now has an instance runner, and HELMET's CI runs on it. Every product in the stack still strongly recommends a git.wayne.edu instance runner, so that capacity stays there.
- [Metrics | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/metrics.md): HELMET can expose a Prometheus metrics endpoint with version, PHP support, request and CSP metrics. Off by default, gated by a bearer token or an IP allow list, with a Grafana dashboard to import.
- [Platform presets | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/platform-presets.md): A preset names a platform's trusted-proxy list, so an app does not hard-code an address that belongs to the platform, not the app.
- [Quick start | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/quick-start.md): A raw PHP app behind the HELMET baseline in four steps: require, boot, verify, nonce.
- [Running off Citadel | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/running-off-citadel.md): HELMET ships one package for every platform, so running off Citadel means changing configuration, not code.
- [The session | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/session.md): SessionHardening::apply() sets the session ini values, including a __Host- prefixed cookie name on HTTPS, before the session starts.
- [Laravel | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-laravel.md): The Laravel adapter is a service provider, two always-on middlewares, an optional request-forgery guard, and a config file.
- [PSR-15 middleware | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-psr15.md): The same core, mounted in a middleware pipeline, sends the identical headers.
- [Raw PHP | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/usage-raw-php.md): An app on raw PHP calls helmet_boot() once at the top of its front controller, before anything is echoed, and is done.
- [WSU values (Playbook) | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/guides/wsu-values.md): The Laravel config reads HELMET_PRESET from the environment first and from the private waynestate/playbook package (Playbook) second, when the environment has no value.
- [Overview | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/index.md): HELMET is the Wayne State app stack's baseline runtime: security headers, a hardened session, an honest proxy check, /up and structured logs.
- [Install | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/install.md): Add waynestate/helmet with Composer, then verify the headers are on the wire.
- [API | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/api.md): The public entry points of the core, from helmet_boot() to helmet_metrics(), plus the middleware and guard around them.
- [Environment variables | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/configuration.md): Every HELMET_ environment variable the package reads, its meaning, its default, and the file that reads it.
- [Proof | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/reference/proof.md): Proof runs against real Wayne State applications are on a private site, proof.apps.wayne.edu/helmet, behind a Wayne State employee sign-in.
- [Troubleshooting | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/troubleshooting.md): What to look at when a header is missing, a proxy is not trusted, or the guard refuses a request that should pass.
- [Upgrading | HELMET docs](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/docs/upgrading.md): How to move an app from one HELMET release to the next.

## Prompts

- [Get started with HELMET](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-get-started): The agent works out your app's shape and where it runs, then writes the smallest plan to add HELMET. It changes nothing yet. The prompt itself is in https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [HELMET in a raw PHP app](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-raw-php): Adds helmet_boot() to the front controller and the nonce to each inline script. If some pages skip the front controller, it adds public/up.php too. The prompt itself is in https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [HELMET in a Laravel app with Blade](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-laravel-blade): Publishes the config, sets the platform and puts the nonce on inline scripts in Blade. Laravel keeps its own /up and its own session settings. The prompt itself is in https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [HELMET in a Laravel app with Inertia and Vue](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-laravel-inertia): The Laravel setup, then a search for what the CSP will break: scripts in Inertia's Head, a second package that makes nonces, and HTML cached across requests. The prompt itself is in https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [HELMET in a PSR-15 middleware pipeline](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-psr15): Adds HealthCheck and SecurityHeadersMiddleware to your pipeline. Your handlers read the nonce from the helmet.csp_nonce attribute. The prompt itself is in https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
